Description
Month: 04

Source Information
Ancestry.com. Canada, Arriving Passengers Lists, 1865-1935 [database on-line]. Provo, UT, USA: Ancestry.com Operations Inc, 2010.
Original data:Passenger Lists, 1865–1935. Microfilm Publications T-479 to T-520, T-4689 to T-4874, T-14700 to T-14938, C-4511 to C-4542. Library and Archives Canada, n.d. RG 76-C. Department of Employment and Immigration fonds. Library and Archives Canada Ottawa, Ontario, Canada.

Source Description
Passenger lists of ships arriving in various Canadian ports as well as some eastern U.S. ports from 1865–1935 are indexed this database. These lists served as the immigration records for Canada between these years and information that is included are surname, age, gender, marital status, destination, occupation, birth country, etc.

Surname is found in St. Nicholas Church records as "Lechiw".

     Left the Port of Antwerp onboard the SS Lake Michigan on March 23, 1910 at the age of 26 years. Arrived in St. John's New Brunswick on April 4, 1910 at 15:30 hours. He was travelling with his brother Dymtro Lechow, age 22 years, and Michael Lechow, age 27 years.

     Onboard the 5340 ton ship were 1108 adults and 171 children under 14 years. Four people were in quarantine. (Microfilm Roll # T4822).

Refered to as "Basilium" of "Shitysho, Radechuw" on St. Nicholas Ukrainian Catholic Church Marriage records to Paraceriam Widecko on August 7, 1913.

Refered to as "Basilio"  of "Kutytsto turanslnie, Brody" in baptism records of son Volosymir on page 189, Volume 14 of Baptisms, St. Nicholas Ukrainian Catholic Church, Winnipeg, Manitoba.

Oiler for CPR in 1915, Car repairman for CPR in 1917, CPR car oiler in 1918;

employee of CPR and residing at 227 Parr Street in 1919,

worked for CPR and lived at 734 Magnus Ave. in 1921;

oiler for CPR residing at 829 Aberdeen in 1922;

oiler for CPR residing at 817 Aberdeen in 1923,

worked for CPR in 1926 and resided at 902 Manitoba Avenue,

oiler for CPR residing at 902 Manitoba Avenue in 1930 Henderson Directory,

worked for CPR and lived at 382 Garlies Street in 1935,

worked for CPR and resided at 382 Garlies Street in 1946 and 1947,

retired at 382 Garlies Street in 1955,

More commonly refered to as "Lechow".
